Rance opens with 'Hi, this is ran with ins. I was just giving you a call back Karen' — an outbound callback on a cancelled job. items_missed: Not applicable — no sales scorecard sections were in play on this call. The rubric's differentiators (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, clock, Save Your Ass, email handoff) have no place on a cancelled-move escalation, so none are counted as misses.
top_strength: Rance held the policy line clearly and did not cave under sustained pressure, which is the correct outcome on an infestation refusal. His best stretch is the substantive 'why' — instead of hiding behind 'it's policy,' he gave the customer the actual reasoning: 'unfortunately my employees are exposed to it, my truck is exposed to it to shut down and truck, and fumigate it, that means our truck can't run for a couple of days, so that means we're not able to service other customers.' He also framed it as protection rather than rejection — 'it risk contamination for future clients' — and used the live-firewood analogy twice to show it is a consistent standard, not a judgment about her. He opened with real empathy ('I hear you. I understand where you're coming from'), he correctly refused to speak to a decision he wasn't part of ('I can't speak to your move a year and a half ago. I wasn't in the position that I'm in'), and he followed through on the one concrete thing she actually wanted, confirming twice that Brian would call: 'I have an email out for Brian to call you... Yes ma'am, I will have him follow up with you.' He also gave her a straight answer on Calvin rather than a soft dodge.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Rance won the policy argument and lost the customer. Around the four-minute mark she had already conceded the point — 'yeah I under, I understand I under I understand. I understand what you're saying' — and that was the moment to stop litigating and start repairing. Instead the call escalated: he cut her off with 'Well, Jacob, wait, wait, wait,' pivoted to proving the crew had communicated ('I know that the crew did talk to you before they left'), instructed her on how to describe Einstein to others ('I hope when you explain to people why we weren't able to do your move. You explain to them the reason why'), and finally landed a sarcastic line — 'I know you have a lot of opinions, I understand that.' That single sentence is the one to pull into a 1:1. What he should have said, once she said she understood, is: 'Karen, you're right that this was handled badly on our end — you cleared your whole day, the crew left without a real explanation or an apology, and nobody warned you this could happen when you rebooked. I'm sorry. The infestation policy isn't something I can move on, but the way you found out about it is on us. I'm getting Brian on the phone with you tomorrow, and I'll make sure he has the full history before he calls.' That concedes nothing on policy and takes the fight out of the call. Second fix: never argue the yelling accusation. She said 'please don't ar at me' and he answered 'I'm not yelling at you, I'm telling actually' and then 'I'm not acting like your criminal' — denials that only prove her point. The move is to lower volume and pace and say 'I'm sorry — let me slow down,' then keep going. Third: 'It sounds like we're not a good fit for your moving situation. I agree with you 100 percent' is functionally firing a repeat customer who told him twice she'd previously had an 'excellent job' from Einstein. Business follow-ups worth Amanda's attention, all sourced from the transcript: (1) she was told twice by Einstein people — 'Calvin assured me that there would be no problem' and per her account a supervisor a year and a half ago approved a move with known roaches — which means the infestation policy is either new, undocumented, or inconsistently applied at intake; (2) the crew left the job site without an apology or explanation per her account ('they just drove off and didn't say I'm sorry'), and Rance's rebuttal rests on Jacob having called, not on the on-site handling; (3) she is an active detractor risk who said 'I'm never gonna use you all again' and 'I would not recommend you all at all' on a job Einstein cancelled day-of, so Brian's callback should be treated as a save attempt, not a courtesy; (4) an infestation screening question at booking would have prevented this entire call.

I understand where you're coming from') but degraded into interrupting ('wait, wait, wait'), arguing the customer's perception back at her ('I'm not yelling at you, I'm telling actually'), and an openly sarcastic close — 'I know you have a lot of opinions, I understand that' — with the customer's name used only once in ten minutes.
